what_it_does_well: Connects mortality counting to resource allocation and explains why even excess-death methods have limits.
who_decides: Registration and health systems determine what can be counted and acted upon.
who_checks: Commentary compares published records and mortality methods; not an original field investigation.

what_it_does_well: Links worker heat to electricity agreements and outages, retaining competing explanations and seeking response.
who_pays: Power tariffs and investment are discussed; disputed payment claims remain attributed.
who_decides: Electricity authorities and plant operators affect supply; factories control indoor protection.
who_checks: Union complaints, cited documents and requests for response are used; allegations are not adjudicated.

what_it_does_well: Returns to a no-payout pilot and asks what redesign and cash layers changed for women.
who_pays: Member contributions and programme support are described; whole long-term financing is not independently audited.
who_decides: SEWA and insurance partners redesign thresholds and assistance.
who_checks: Reporters revisit previous results and hear worker experiences; a causal impact evaluation is not presented.

what_it_does_well: Connects specific fainting incidents with corrective orders, inspection demands and a request for clarification.
who_pays: Factories are asked to improve conditions; actual expenditure not disclosed.
who_decides: Labour authorities issue orders; employers implement; unions call for stronger inspections.
who_checks: Unions question compliance; ministry clarification is sought. Completed inspection findings are not established.

what_it_does_well: Explains trigger setting, premium subsidy and the trade-off between wider eligibility and payment size.
who_pays: Women contribute to premiums; programme subsidy covers part, as reported.
who_decides: Insurers and risk modellers set parameters; implementing organisations negotiate changes.
who_checks: Researchers test assumptions and call for regulatory scrutiny; no completed regulator audit is shown.

what_it_does_well: Combines worker-collected exposure data, factory responses, legal standards and an undisclosed-budget question.
who_pays: Factory describes infrastructure spending; actual budget is not disclosed.
who_decides: Managers control equipment and production; public bodies set rules.
who_checks: Reporters compare measurements and worker accounts with employer statements and regulatory documents.
